svg.title: How a three-prong soil sensor works
svg.desc: Cutaway of a field: a three-prong soil probe is buried about 6 inches deep in the root zone and wired to a sensor node on a stake. Callouts explain that the probe measures soil moisture (volumetric water content) by sensing how the soil between the prongs holds an electric field, electrical conductivity (how easily a tiny current flows between the prongs, which rises with salts and nutrients), and soil temperature from a sensor inside the probe. The node sends readings over LoRaWAN radio to a gateway, then to a dashboard and a phone alert.
